GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Wave A attacks the opening trajectory because Stage 0 measured it as the dominant cost: ~809 ms of mount inside an ~890 ms open at the 1 MB shape, with parse at ~20 ms (recorded parse_proxy) and derived work cheap (serialization ~3.8 ms at 1 MB, word count ~1 ms, TOC under 0.01 ms). Fixing parse or derived work first would leave the user-facing block untouched; the contract's wave order (Wave A progressive mount, then B1/B2, B3 last) encodes that evidence. The architecture is region-based rather than character-offset-based because Mark's advantage over the external blueprint is the parsed block tree: muya already knows the top-level block boundaries before mounting, so split points are exact and no heuristic scanning is needed. The toggle ships default-off and session-latched because the contract's experimental access model requires it and because a progressive mount changes what users see during the first seconds of a large document — that deserves a soak on the experimental path before any default-flip proposal, which is a separately approved change by contract.

ExternalDigest.Name: Claude Code 2.1.312 markdown-stack research digest
ExternalDigest.Note: Exploratory reverse-engineering of a third-party binary (methods and byte offsets documented in the report). Design reference only: mechanisms adapted, no code copied, no numeric threshold inherited without its own Stage 0 grounding. The report's large-document-relevant findings distilled below; its other findings (table formatter, diff colors, link hygiene, daltonism themes, HTML import, file versioning) are outside this line and stay with the owner's backlog decisions.

Stage0Evidence.Item: Committed corpus and generators: tests/e2e/fixtures/large-doc/ (mixed-100k, size-1mb, size-1_7mb-9000sections, pathological and semantic-edge shapes, byte-policy matrix with shape-metadata.json).
Recorded baselines and cost breakdowns: src/renderer/bench/baseline/ (capture-baseline.mjs and per-shape artifacts).
Acceptance protocol already carrying time_to_input_ms as a BLOCK_OPEN capture field: src/renderer/bench/acceptance/ (capture-template.json, verify-capture.mjs).
Characterization oracle suites (the equivalence oracle for this change): tests/e2e/perf/ and tests/renderer/perf/ as landed by C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0.

Mechanism.Name: frozen chunks
Mechanism.Adaptation: Mark's frozen region is the mounted prefix of the block tree: blocks above the furthest mount boundary are mounted once and never re-mounted while the document stays above that boundary; muya's existing per-block update machinery already keeps edited blocks correct without touching siblings, which is the same property the blueprint builds by hand. The 4096-character threshold is not inherited: Mark's freeze boundary is structural (block count and viewport margin), sized at plan time from the corpus, not a character count.

Mechanism.Name: safe split points
Mechanism.Observed: The cut point prefers a newline at distance, then a space, then a hard cut shifted off surrogate pairs (codePointAt 0xD800-0xDFFF check) so emoji are never halved; an open code fence makes the tail raw code; unclosed links/HTML suppress link wrapping.
Mechanism.Adaptation: Mark does not need the heuristic ladder: split points are top-level block boundaries from the parsed tree. The surrogate-pair rule still binds wherever text is sliced (validated offsets), and the open-fence rule maps to extending the synchronous region past an unresolved construct instead of splitting inside it.

Mechanism.Name: prefix-mismatch reset
Mechanism.Observed: If the text no longer starts with the frozen source (edit or rollback above the boundary), all streaming state resets and rendering restarts.
Mechanism.Adaptation: The same escape hatch, bounded: revalidate the affected region and remount it; the worst case is one full progressive-state reset completing the open through the legacy mount — never a wedged editor.

Mechanism.Name: resilience belts
Mechanism.Observed: Four belts around the parser: a fast-path "is this markdown" regex, a depth guard (100) via tokenizer overrides, a render traversal budget (300 elements / 64 deep, flattening beyond), and a RangeError catch that degrades the block to plain text so the UI never crashes.
Mechanism.Adaptation: Wave A adopts the belts that protect the mount: a depth/traversal guard on mounting (flatten oversize subtrees) and a catch-all fallback to the legacy mount. The fast-path regex and token LRU cache are deliberately not adopted — Stage 0 measured Mark's parse as cheap (recorded parse_proxy: 5–11 ms at the ordinary ~100 KB shape, ~20 ms at the 1 MB shape), so those belts solve a cost Mark does not have on this path; they are recorded here for any future change that makes parsing hot again.

Mechanism.Name: two-layer rendering
Mechanism.Observed: The same token stream feeds a rich component layer and a flat string layer (windowed mode, copy, screen readers).
Mechanism.Adaptation: Not needed as an architecture: Mark already has one render tree plus copy/export readers. The equivalence goal (R-7) is the local equivalent — every reader and consumer must observe identical output under both mount paths.

AlternativesRejected.Alternative: Rejected: it hides layout cost but not mount/DOM-construction cost, is already a separate default-off experiment, and cannot deliver the time-to-input budget by itself.
Rejected as Wave D scope: it changes scroll, search, copy and export semantics across the product; progressive mount delivers the contract budgets without redefining any reader.
Rejected: parse is measured-cheap and whole-document parse keeps every existing oracle trivially intact; chunking it would add correctness risk for no budget gain.

Alternative.Name: shipping progressive mount on by default

AlternativesRejected.Alternative: Rejected by contract: the experimental access model is default-off and session-latched until a separately approved default flip; this change does not propose that flip.

Rejected: the source's numbers (4096 freeze, 2048/1536 split distances, depth 100, 300/64 traversal, 500-entry LRU) describe a terminal renderer on different constraints; every Wave A number is either grounded in the Stage 0 baseline or explicitly an owner decision (R-5).
